text:
Anjali: Quick heads up — saw a latency spike in canary for the prefill-affinity batcher when prefix cache hit rate is ~70%. p95 jumped ~40ms compared to baseline, p50 up ~12ms. Repro steps and perf snippet below.

Leo: Hmm that sounds like the cache-hit path is forcing a different packing shape. Can you paste the profiler output? :eyes:

Anjali: Copying the hot slices from the sampling run:```
perf summary (canary-2026-03-16):
  p50: 28ms -> 40ms (+12)
  p95: 85ms -> 125ms (+40)
  hot functions: batch_formation.cpp:112 (+18ms), kv_cache_lookup.cpp:54 (+6ms), kernel_selector.cpp:78 (+10ms)
  note: many requests show small seqlen after prefix hit, but batcher still waits to fill token_budget target
```

Mike: My hunch: when prefix cache hits shorten the generation portion, the continuous batcher still tries to reach the same token_budget which increases headroom wait. With shorter model work per request we underutilize the GPU but add queue time.

Drew: Agreed. Also check kernel_selector: it sometimes picks a larger matmul kernel optimized for longer sequences. If sequence length distribution shifts left (due to cache), kernel switch can regress throughput for short runs.

Anjali: Found this in logs:```
[batcher] token_budget_target=256
[batcher] max_hold_ms=20
[kernel_selector] chosen_kernel=matmul_A_block32
[request] seqlen_after_prefix=16
[request] kv_hit=true
```

Leo: So two levers: reduce token_budget_target when kv_hit ratio high, and enable hit-aware packing that switches to short-seq kernel. We should avoid toggling kernel at request time too often though.

Mike: Proposed quick experiment for canary:
```
# canary config override
batcher.token_budget_target=96
batcher.max_hold_ms=8
batcher.hit_aware_packing=true
kernel_selector.short_seq_favored=true
```
Start with that for a small subset and collect p50/p95 and utilization.

Drew: Add tracing tags: batcher.mode, kv_hit=true/false, chosen_kernel. Need those to attribute regression precisely.

Anjali: I'll patch canary with the override and add tracing. Rolling out to 5% now.

Ops-Bot: deploy triggered: canary/config-overrides/2026-03-16-1938 -> target 5% :rocket:

Leo: If we see lower latency but GPU utilization drops too much, we can try adaptive token_budget that scales with short_seq_fraction (e.g., target = base * max(0.5, short_frac)).

Mike: Also worth running microbench of the two kernel variants with seqlen in [8,32] to quantify per-token cost. I can run on a dedicated GPU instance.

Drew: Timeline: Anjali + Mike collect perf in 30m, then we reconvene. If good, promote to 25% and notify SRE. If not, revert config and try max_hold_ms tuning.

Anjali: Got initial numbers after 20m: p50 down to 30ms (from 40), p95 down to 95ms (from 125). GPU util dropped ~7% but tokens/sec stayed roughly same. Posting full trace in the thread. :thumbsup:

Leo: Nice. Please attach kernel microbench before we change kernel_selector globally.

Mike: Will run microbench and upload soon. Also adding a small safety: hit_aware_packing only enabled when kv_hit_rate > 0.5 and in <=50% rollout.

Drew: Good call. Putting action items: 1) Mike: kernel microbench (seqlen 8/16/32) 2) Anjali: expand canary to 25% if numbers hold 3) Leo: PR for adaptive token_budget algorithm 4) Ops: monitor rollback alerts.

Anjali: Thanks all — will update thread with traces and the canary link.
